messages.subject: Rattle 2.6.11 Released
messages.body_plain:
Rattle 2.6.11 is now on the master CRAN node and is propagating.

Start up R and:

> library(rattle)
> install.packages(rattleInfo())

The main update is a fix for those using Mac OS/X (a version number bug).

There is also some minor internal code cleanup.

Regards,
Graham

messages.subject: R library link problems
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

There is a problem with R Rattle packages gfortran compilation, under Debian Linux. The compilation message error is :

/usr/bin/ld: cannot find -lgfortran

/usr/bin/ld: cannot find -lquadmath

So some crucial Rattle packages like SVM cannot be build.

In fact, the problem is that links to those library are not set for this version. You can see there with the command :

$ sudo ldconfig -p | grep libgfortran

libgfortran.so.3 (libc6,x86-64) => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgfortran.so.3

So just create some symbolic links to them under /usr/lib repertory, then a sudo ldconfig to reload, and that's ok.

$ sudo ln -s /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgfortran.so.3 /usr/lib/libgfortran.so

$ sudo ln -s /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libquadmath.so.0 /usr/lib/libquadmath.so

$ sudo ldconfig

Well, also, I use neural network a lots, and it will be great if we could have more options with it (I must use R commands to set them if not).

Thanks,

messages.subject: Re: R library link problems
messages.body_plain:
Hi Igor,

Thanks for the report of the issue.

On 8 October 2011 05:15, igor gregovitch <d.ba...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi,
>
> There is a problem with R Rattle packages gfortran compilation, under Debian
> Linux. The compilation message error is :
>
> /usr/bin/ld: cannot find -lgfortran
>
> /usr/bin/ld: cannot find -lquadmath

That is odd.

A similar issue is often because some "-dev" packages are not
installed but I don't think that is the case here.

Specifically, which package was Rattle (or you) attempting to install?

> So some crucial Rattle packages like SVM cannot be build.

I've tested reinstalling the kernlab package and that compiles on my
Ubuntu servers. (I use kernlab to provide the SVM functionality in
Rattle.)

> In fact, the problem is that links to those library are not set for this
> version. You can see there with the command :
>
> $ sudo ldconfig -p | grep libgfortran
>
> libgfortran.so.3 (libc6,x86-64) =>
> /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgfortran.so.3

I get this also on my Ubuntu boxes.

> So just create some symbolic links to them under /usr/lib repertory, then a
> sudo ldconfig to reload, and that's ok.
>
> $ sudo ln -s /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgfortran.so.3
> /usr/lib/libgfortran.so

On my system:

$ ls /usr/lib/libgfortran*
ls: cannot access /usr/lib/libgfortran*: No such file or directory

So I don't seem to need these links.

> $ sudo ln -s /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libquadmath.so.0
> /usr/lib/libquadmath.so
>
> $ sudo ldconfig

And did the install then work? Seems odd that you need to do that,
given that ldconfig is already finding them?

> Well, also, I use neural network a lots, and it will be great if we could
> have more options with it (I must use R commands to set them if not).

What options would you like?

The options that get into the interface are driven by what people find
they commonly need - so let me know what you would commonly need.

Regards,
Graham

messages.subject: Re: R library link problems
messages.body_plain:
Thanks for the details Igor. It looks like your "sid" (unstable)
installation is broken.

The issue looks to be with R (or sid) rather than Rattle. Try

$ R
[...]
> install.packages(kernlab)

to hopefully replicate the error, to eliminate rattle.

If other packages have the same issue you may have a broken
installation of Debian.

You could check https://stat.ethz.ch/mailman/listinfo/r-sig-debian but
a quick look does not indicate any others having issues with sid.

If the problem persists then it may be useful to post to that mailing list.

Thanks for the neuralnet pointer. I'll have a look as time permits to
adding this functionality.

Regards,
Graham

messages.subject: problem in Win XP environment
messages.body_plain:
I seem to have created a problem for myself.  Wishing to upgrade my version of R and Rattle, I proceeded to uninstall R 2.12 via the control panel.  I then deleted the R folder.  R2.13 was installed without issue.  Starting R yields Fatal Error: Unable to restore data saved in .RData.  The R console states error in loadNamespace(name) : there is no package called 'rattle'.  The R control automatically closes and there is no opportunity to re-install R.  If I again remove R and look for an RData file there is none.

Would be grateful if anyone could help me out of the mess I created.  Any links on how to remove all traces of R from Windows XP drive and registry?

Thank you,
Bob A.

messages.subject: Re: problem in Win XP environment
messages.body_plain:
Hi Bob,

I think this happens when you have saved the workspace from R (which
is saved into a .RData file), and in the new version of R it is trying
to load this and notices that the rattle package is required but not
installed. The usual solution is to find any .RData file and delete -
though you suggest you have done that - but the error message suggests
there is still one there - is it possible that you have missed one
somewhere (where R starts up)?

Alternatively, does the following work on MS/Windows?

$ R --vanilla

That will avoid loading the saved workspace, and hopefully allow you
to install rattle, then the next R session should be okay?

Regards,
Graham

messages.subject: Re: OOB question
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ak,

Rattle does not directly support plotting the ROC of the OOB scoring
from randomForest. You would need to collect the OOB predictions and
plot them using ROCR. Instead, Rattle supports a separate hold-out
dataset for the unbiased performance estimates.

The randomForest output in Rattle does include the OOB error estimate
(page 251 of the Rattle book). Also page 260 talks about the OOB error
rates.

Regards,
Graham

messages.subject: Re: OOB question
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ak,

Not all model builders use an OOB in R. Rattle allows you to use a
hold-out dataset (a test or validate dataset) for plotting unbiased
expected performance, using the same train/test/validate datasets
across different model builders.

However, as you note, predict.randomForest() returns the OOB scores
and so you can get the OOB ROC with the following (you were close!):

> crs$pr <- predict(crs$rf, type="prob")[,2]
> pred<-prediction(crs$pr, crs$dataset[crs$sample, crs$target])
> perf<- performance(pred,"tpr","fpr")
> plot(perf, col=4, add=TRUE)

This is probably an option I should work into Rattle somehow.

Regards,
Graham

> I am new to R and have been trying to look for way to plot these curves and
> have had no luck.
> i looked at the log using rattle and was trying to find a way to collect the
> OOB predictions but had no luck.
> This is what i came up with
> crs$pr<-predict(crs$rf,type='prob')[,2]
> pred<-prediction(crs$pr)
> perf<- performance(pred,"tpr","fpr")
> plot(perf, col=4, add=TRUE)
> I believe the predict() method of randomForest can only give OOB predictions
> (when newdata arguments is not give) but not sure how to do that from the
> data in rattle.
> I would really really appreciated any help you have with this.
> Ak
